name: ET Kathy Bossier Pipeline
monitor_reason: endpoints: only state (TX) sourced; single EIA source, in-service date unreliable
researcher_notes: The August 2026 EIA release lists ET Kathy Bossier Pipeline on the Historical Projects sheet, Excel row 331: Energy Transfer Co, new pipeline, completed, 78 miles, 36 inch, 500 MMcf/d, intrastate in Texas, in service July 2004. It is an operating line, not a proposal, and no GEM row carries it by name; only the aggregate Texas Intrastate System row (P0264) exists. A web search summary mentions a 78-mile mostly 36-inch Energy Transfer Bossier Pipeline connecting to the Katy Pipeline in Grimes County, Texas, serving Bossier Sand gas, with about 400,000 mcf per day committed. That suggests it came into service around 2008, not 2004, but the page could not be loaded for verification, so it is not cited. No start point, end point or route was found. It meets the length rule but lacks sourced endpoints and a second source. Intrastate, so FERC silence is not a concern; the Texas Railroad Commission could be checked for a T-4 permit. Owner would be Energy Transfer (entity lookup not completed). Confidence low.
